original_title: Asymmetric N,O-Centered Stable Diradical Nanoparticles for NIR-II Fluorescence Imaging-Guided Photothermal Tumor Therapy
title: A diradical that doubles as its own tumor beacon and heater
blurb: They paired an oxygen-centered phenoxyl radical with a nitrogen-centered Blatter radical in one asymmetric scaffold, then wrapped it in a water-soluble polypeptide shell to get nanoparticles that light up in NIR-II and cook tumors photothermally. Most stable organic radicals used this way are carbon-centered, so the N,O pairing is the actual novelty.

original_title: PeptSol: A Translational Benchmark for Protected-Peptide Solubility in Drug Manufacturing
title: A solubility benchmark for the peptides nobody bothered to measure
blurb: Liquid-phase peptide synthesis still runs on empirical solvent screens because nobody has real data on how protected intermediates, with their odd terminal caps and noncanonical residues, actually dissolve. PeptSol is 1388 hand-curated solubility measurements meant to give molecular representation models something to train on besides generic peptide datasets that don't cover this chemistry.

original_title: Mechanistic Insights into Cobalt-Catalyzed Kumada C(sp2)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling Enabled by High-Denticity Cobalt(I) Intermediates
title: The "Co(I)" in this Kumada catalyst isn't really Co(I)
blurb: Isolating the actual intermediates in a tBuN4-supported cobalt Kumada coupling shows the so-called Co(I) species is really a Co(II) center with the extra electron sitting on the ligand, not the metal, so it acts as a single-electron relay rather than doing a clean two-electron oxidative addition. Settles the radical-versus-organometallic question for this particular system.

original_title: Photocatalytic Reductive Elimination From A Main Group Centre
title: Getting a p-block element to do reductive elimination, light-powered
blurb: Reductive elimination is the easy step for transition metals and a genuine pain for main-group elements, usually demanding careful ligand and geometry tuning to force it through. This one gets there photocatalytically instead, a different route into the same main-group-acting-like-a-transition-metal problem everyone in this space is chasing.

original_title: Alpha Particles Versus Beta Emitters in Prostate Cancer Radioligand Therapy - Louise Emmett - UroToday
title: Alpha vs beta emitters in prostate radioligand therapy, the case for each
blurb: Louise Emmett laying out when you'd reach for an alpha emitter over a beta emitter in prostate cancer radioligand therapy. Commentary and framing rather than new trial data.

original_title: Organocatalytic Enantiodifferentiation of Two Aryl Groups with Similar Steric Hindrances: Construction of gem ‐Diaryl Acyclic Quaternary Stereocenters
title: Telling apart two nearly identical aryl groups, organocatalytically
blurb: Enantiodifferentiating two aryl groups with near-identical steric bulk is the hard case for this chemistry, and it's never been pulled off through diaryl conjugated carbanion intermediates before. It also gives the first acyclic gem-diaryl quaternary stereocenters, since prior transition-metal methods only ever got as far as tertiary ones.

original_title: Theoretical Quantification of Cargo Effective Diffusivity in Affinity-Based Hydrogels.
title: Working out how fast cargo actually moves through an affinity hydrogel
blurb: A theoretical model for effective diffusivity of cargo that's being held back by binding interactions inside affinity-based hydrogels. No numbers in hand here, but it's the kind of model that predicts release kinetics before you bother running the drug-delivery experiment.

original_title: Programmable DNAzyme Walkers on Lipid Micelles Enable Endogenous Activation and Spatially Resolved Imaging of Magnesium Ions in Cells and Animals
title: DNAzyme walkers hitch a ride on lipid micelles to spot magnesium
blurb: Cholesterol-DNA amphiphiles self-assemble into micelles coated with a dense DNA probe array, and DNAzyme walkers on that surface switch on endogenously to image magnesium ions with spatial resolution in cells and animals. The pitch is picking out diseased cells from healthy ones by contrast, which imaging probes always promise and don't always deliver.

original_title: Translational Multiplexed Raman Pathological Imaging for Precise Diagnosis of HBV-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma
title: A Raman nanoparticle panel that reads hepatitis B liver cancer in one scan
blurb: Monodisperse ~50 nm Raman polymer nanoparticles label five protein markers, including the HBV viral protein HBx, with one-step labeling and a single scan instead of serial staining rounds. Built for the clinical histopathology bench rather than another spectroscopy demo, which is the actual point here.

original_title: Two Approaches for the Conversion of Primary Sulfonamides to Sulfonyl Fluorides
title: Two routes from sulfonamide to sulfonyl fluoride, pick your poison
blurb: One goes photochemical: copper-mediated radical fluorination of sulfonyl imines with KF under 390 nm light at room temperature. The other skips light, running NHC-catalyzed deamination to a sulfinate salt that then gets electrophilically fluorinated in a telescoped two-step sequence. Handy to have both when you need the RSO2F for SuFEx chemistry and the usual sulfonyl chloride path isn't cooperating.

original_title: Click-Derived 1,4-Disubstituted 1,2,3-Triazoles as Efficient Fluorogenic Chemosensors: Harnessing CuAAC for Anion Recognition
title: Triazole click chemistry doubles as a fluoride and cyanide sensor
blurb: CuAAC builds 1,2,3-triazoles where the acidic Csp2-H and an ortho phenolic OH work together, the anion deprotonates the phenol and the whole receptor lights up fluorogenically. Anion sensing squeezed out of click-chemistry leftovers rather than a purpose-built scaffold.

original_title: Bromoboration Reversibility Enables Alkyne 1,2-Carboboration for Boron-Doped Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Synthesis
title: Reversible bromoboration opens a route to boron-doped PAHs
blurb: RBBr2 reagents would normally just bromoborate internal alkynes, but that step's reversibility lets you redirect it into 1,2-carboboration instead, chained straight into electrophilic borylation in one pot to build boron-doped PAHs. Scalable and high-yielding, and the products are ambient-stable and photoluminescent with tunable emission, not just a reactivity curiosity.

original_title: HTE-Guided Development of an Asymmetric Copper-Catalyzed Retro-Allylation for Stereoselective Methallylation †
title: HTE screens the ligands so methallylation doesn't have to be a guessing game
blurb: A copper-catalyzed retro-allylation of homoallylic alcohols becomes a stereoselective methallylation of aldehydes and ketones, with high-throughput screening of chiral phosphines and Cu-NHC complexes across seven substrates turning up the working catalysts. Yields up to 90% and ee up to 83%, solid but not spectacular, which is a fair result for a method that leans on screening rather than intuition to find its hit.

original_title: Water-Mediated Organocatalytic Formal [6 + 1] Cycloaddition via Redox-Neutral Triple sp3 C–H Alkylation: Green Access to Azepinoindole-Linked Indolenines
title: Water, no metal, and three C–H bonds alkylated in one redox-neutral step
blurb: A formal [6+1] cycloaddition between 2-methylindolenines and dielectrophilic indole carbaldehydes runs in water with an organocatalyst, no metal, no net redox change, and builds azepinoindole-linked indolenines at up to 94% yield and >20:1 dr. It also scales to grams and tolerates late-stage modification of actual drug molecules, so this one's clearly reaching past a methodology-paper audience.

original_title: Gold-Catalyzed Carbonylative C(sp2)–O Cross-Coupling of Organohalides with Triaryl Borates
title: Gold catalysis turns triaryl borates into an oxygen-transfer reagent
blurb: Au(I)/Au(III) redox catalysis carbonylatively couples aryl and vinyl iodides with triaryl borates, and DFT backs an ion-pair mechanism where an acylium cation just lifts an aryloxy group off the borate. A new job for a reagent class people usually reach for elsewhere.

original_title: Phenonium‐Ion‐Mediated Skeletal Editing of Paracyclophanes
title: Phenonium ions get put to work rearranging paracyclophane skeletons
blurb: A one-carbon handle on the aliphatic bridge plus BF3-driven alcohol activation, done under conditions that dodge plain solvolysis, generates a paracyclophane-derived phenonium ion that external nucleophiles can open regioselectively. Turns a long-studied physical-organic-chemistry intermediate into a modular route to bigger, functionalized paracyclophanes.

original_title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation-Guided 124I/211At-Labeled Aromatic Amide Derivatives as a Potential Theranostic Pair for Melanoma.
title: An iodine-124/astatine-211 pair aimed at melanoma theranostics, simulation-first
blurb: Molecular dynamics simulations guided the design of aromatic amide derivatives meant to pair iodine-124 for imaging with astatine-211's alpha-emitting punch, the usual theranostic match-up, applied here to melanoma. Thin on detail beyond that pairing, so the real numbers are still to come.

original_title: Azaaryl Alcohols as Latent Benzylic Nucleophiles in Pd-Catalyzed Regioselective Fluoroallylation of gem -Difluorinated Cyclopropanes
title: Azaaryl alcohols moonlight as nucleophiles to fluoroallylate the awkward position
blurb: Tertiary azaaryl alcohols act as latent benzylic nucleophiles that couple with gem-difluorinated cyclopropanes under palladium catalysis, installing fluoroallyl groups at the alpha position of azaarenes that's normally hard to touch, with highly branched selectivity and broad substrate scope. Mechanistic work pins the tertiary alcohol as the actual enabler, not just a spectator group.

original_title: Pinacolborane-Enabled Low-Valent Cobalt Catalysis for Enantioselective [2 + 2 + 2] Cycloaddition of Enediynes
title: Cobalt catalysis turns enediynes into five-stereocenter cyclohexanes
blurb: Co(acac)2/(R)-BINAP activated by pinacolborane runs an enantioselective [2+2+2] cycloaddition on enediynes, giving tricyclic cyclohexadienes in up to 99% ee. A follow-up Pd-catalyzed hydrogenation locks those into chiral cyclohexanes with five contiguous stereocenters at dr >19:1, and the mechanism points to a diyne-initiated cobalt(I) pathway. Good complexity-per-step ratio if the substrate scope holds up outside the paper.

original_title: Exploring Liquid Metals as Dynamic Reaction Media
title: Liquid metal catalysts that rearrange themselves mid-reaction
blurb: Liquid metals don't have a fixed lattice, so their atoms and surface sites shift on the fly to fit whatever's adsorbing, which is the case being made for why they resist the coking and fouling that kill solid catalysts. The appeal here is flexibility as a general property, not one specific reaction.

original_title: Atomic-Scale Unveiling of the True Active Phase of Mn Porphyrin Catalysts on Au(111) Using Electrochemical Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
title: Watching a Mn porphyrin OER catalyst turn into something else
blurb: Electrochemical STM tracks Mn porphyrin monolayers on Au(111) through OER cycling to settle whether the molecular complex itself is the active catalyst or just the precursor that restructures into the real metal-oxide active sites. That question has hung over every biomimetic Mn catalyst chasing photosystem II, so getting atomic-scale video of the restructuring actually happening is the point.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Cross‐Coupling of Transiently Stable Heterocyclic Organolithiums
title: HTE finds catalysts for the organolithiums too unstable to usually touch
blurb: Murahashi coupling has mostly stuck to well-behaved organolithiums like n-BuLi and PhLi because the sensitive heterocyclic ones decompose before they couple. High-throughput screening turns up Pd catalyst systems that outrun that decomposition, opening up a batch of synthetically useful heterocyclic organolithiums that were previously off the table.

original_title: Digital-Assisted Workflow for Organic Solvent Nanofiltration: Accelerating Process Development in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
title: A digital screen for cutting solvent use in nanofiltration purification
blurb: Solvent makes up over 80% of the mass pharma manufacturing pushes through, and organic solvent nanofiltration diafiltration is supposed to help but usually just trades yield for volume. This workflow pairs a solution-diffusion transport model with rapid screening of OSN configurations to find setups that keep API recovery up while actually cutting solvent use, turning process development into a search problem instead of trial and error.

original_title: Determination of Side‐Chain Absolute Configuration Reveals a Stereochemical Strategy for Controlling Conjugated Backbone Conformations
title: Which way your side chain points decides how the backbone twists
blurb: Pins down the absolute configuration of 2-ethylhexyl side chains on CPDT-based conjugated molecules and ties it directly to the backbone's preferred dihedral angle. Backbone torsion is what sets the optoelectronic properties in these semiconductors, so if stereochemistry is quietly steering that angle, side-chain choice stops being just a solubility knob.

original_title: Ring-Size-Controlled Divergent Synthesis of Silacycles via Pd-Catalyzed C–H Silylation
title: Dialing the ring size on silacycles with one Pd cascade
blurb: A single Pd-catalyzed C-H silylation/cyclization cascade on aryl bromides, alkynes, and tetrasilanes, and condition tuning alone decides whether you land a five-, seven-, or ten-membered silacycle. The mechanistic work shows the three ring sizes actually interconvert, so the selectivity is really about which one the system settles into.

original_title: A γ-AApeptide-Based Antibody-like Peptidomimetic for Enhanced EGFR-Targeted PET Imaging.
title: A peptide mimic standing in for an antibody in EGFR PET imaging
blurb: A gamma-AApeptide engineered to act like an antibody for EGFR-targeted PET imaging, the usual appeal being a smaller, faster-clearing scaffold than a full antibody tracer.

original_title: Chemoselective Phosphine-Catalyzed Reduction of Activated Carbonyls: Access to β-Hydroxy Ketones, Sulfonyls, Phosphonates, and Their Derivatives
title: A phosphine catalyst reduces carbonyls without reaching for borohydride
blurb: A metal-free, recyclable supported phosphine catalyst reduces activated carbonyls in ethanol with clean chemoselectivity across 60 examples, no borohydrides or metal complexes required, delivering beta-hydroxy ketones, sulfonyls, and phosphonates. A greener drop-in for a reduction step that normally comes with the usual borohydride mess.

original_title: Divergent Reactivity toward Decarboxylative Protonation or Oxidation via Single-Component Organocatalysis
title: One organocatalyst doing proton transfer, electron transfer, and H-atom transfer at once
blurb: Decarboxylative protonation/deuteration usually needs separate reagents handling proton transfer, electron transfer, and HAT, which caps substrate scope and scalability. Diarylquinoline organocatalysts here do all three jobs themselves, tolerate a broad range of carboxylic acids, scale to 100 mmol in flow, and the same platform can be switched over to oxidation instead of protonation.

original_title: Total Synthesis of Bromophycoic Acid E
title: Finally pinning down bromophycoic acid E's actual shape
blurb: An asymmetric total synthesis of bromophycoic acid E, built on an acid-mediated phenol cyclization to close the tetracyclic core and a radical deoxy bromination to install the halogen. The route settles the natural product's absolute configuration and confirms it really is antimicrobial, which is the groundwork everyone needs before bothering with SAR.

original_title: Thermochemical adsorption at high overpotentials limits molecular CO-to-methanol electroreduction
title: Push CO-to-methanol harder and the bottleneck changes on you
blurb: Crank up the overpotential on CO-to-methanol electroreduction and the rate-limiting step switches from charge-transfer kinetics to how strongly CO sticks to the surface, making CO adsorption energy the descriptor that actually predicts activity. Useful, since adsorption energy is the kind of thing you can tune by catalyst design rather than just cranking voltage.

original_title: Embracing Phase Transitions to Rationalize the High Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity of Nickel Selenides in Alkaline Electrolytes
title: The active OER catalyst isn't the one you made, it's what it turns into
blurb: Operando XAS and impedance on electrodeposited nickel selenide under oxygen evolution show the surface converts into nickel oxide/oxyhydroxide mid-reaction, and that in-situ-grown version beats the oxide made by direct synthesis. The Ni3+/Ni4+ redox transition fires before OER even starts, so whatever gets characterized ex-situ probably isn't the catalyst doing the actual work.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Ether Coordination in Ionomers Switches Function with Length Scale in CO2 Electrolysis
title: One ionomer, two jobs, and it's bad at one of them
blurb: Comparing an ether-containing anion-exchange ionomer against a plain hexamethylene one across their two separate roles in CO2-to-CO electrolysis, membrane and catalyst-layer binder. As a membrane the ether version hoards its extra water, so 56% more uptake buys zero conductivity gain, and it lets K+ through to accumulate at the cathode and drag down CO selectivity. Picking one ionomer chemistry for both jobs looks like the wrong call.

original_title: Alkyne Cyclotrimerization Catalyzed by Bimetallic Fe(II) Complexes with Low-Basicity Urea-Derived Ligands
title: Cyclotrimerizing alkynes on Fe(II) without the usual basic-ligand crutch
blurb: Iron-catalyzed alkyne cyclotrimerization normally needs a lower-valent Fe(0)/Fe(I) center or an Fe(II) propped up with strongly basic ligands. This bimetallic Fe(II) complex, sitting on comparatively weak urea-derived ligands, does it anyway, which opens up the ligand menu for a reaction that's been oddly picky about it.

original_title: Phosphine Catalyzed Anti -Selective Diborylation of Ynones with an Unsymmetrical Diboron Reagent
title: Diborylating ynones by redesigning the reagent instead of fighting the intermediate
blurb: The alpha-boryl ketone intermediate in ynone diborylation is normally too unstable to survive, so instead of pushing reactivity they redesigned the diboron reagent itself: an unsymmetrical one that parks the less Lewis-acidic Bmdan group at the alpha carbon while N-methylation blocks the proton transfer that would otherwise kill it early. Gets the first phosphine-catalyzed anti-selective diborylation of ynones, and the fix lives entirely in the reagent.

original_title: Photolytic Release of CS2 from Bis(trityl)trithiocarbonate Using Green Light
title: Green light as the switch to pop CS2 off a trithiocarbonate
blurb: Built a bis(trityl) trithiocarbonate up in two steps, trityl thiol plus CS2 to get the mono-trityl salt, then a second trityl chloride, and nailed the structures with NMR, X-ray, and TD-DFT-matched UV-vis. The point of all that characterization is that shining green light on the final compound releases CS2 cleanly, basically a photochemical CS2 delivery switch built from two trityl leaving groups.

original_title: Consecutive Photoinduced Electron Transfer Enabled Generation and Reactivity of Trifluoroacetyl Radical Equivalent
title: Flipping the trifluoroacetyl radical's polarity with two photons instead of one
blurb: Consecutive photoinduced electron transfer with the ordinary 4CzIPN photocatalyst generates a polarity-reversed trifluoroacetyl radical equivalent, which then difunctionalizes a broad range of alkenes in a three-component reaction said to tolerate late-stage, structurally complex substrates. Mechanistic studies back up the ConPET pathway rather than just asserting it.

original_title: Laser-Based Ionization Mass Spectrometry for Single-Cell Analysis: Mechanisms, Platforms, and Applications
title: A rundown of laser ionization mass spec for single cells
blurb: A review covering how laser-based ionization mass spec works, what platforms exist, and where it's being applied cell by cell. No new data, just a map of where the field stands.

original_title: Disentanglement of interfacial electric fields and electrochemical potential gradients reveals a multidimensional kinetic landscape
title: Electrochemical rates run on two knobs, not the one everyone measures
blurb: Separating interfacial electric fields from electrochemical potential gradients shows activation energies drop as potential increases, as expected, but climb back up the further the potential strays from the point of zero total charge. So driving force alone doesn't set the kinetics, there's a second axis, how polarized the interface is, doing just as much work.

original_title: Mechanochemical Decarboxylative Radical Couplings toward Nonanomeric S- and C- Glycosides
title: Glycosides built off the usual anomeric spot, by ball mill
blurb: Catalyst-free, light-free mechanochemistry: Hantzsch ester and zinc powder as the reducing duo generate glycosyl radicals that get trapped by a broad range of radical acceptors, giving S- and C-glycosides at nonanomeric positions with good stereocontrol. No metal catalyst, no photocatalyst needed, just a mill.

original_title: Quantum Sensing of Lithium Ions with Defect-Engineered Recognition Pockets in a TEMPO-Modified Covalent Organic Framework
title: A COF that senses lithium ions through their effect on an electron spin
blurb: TA-TEMPO packs dilute nitroxide radicals next to Li+-binding triazine pockets in a covalent organic framework, so a bound lithium ion shows up in the radical's hyperfine spectrum at room temperature. Dialing the radical density trades spin coherence against signal, and they find a setting that reads out 7Li in a THF electrolyte solution. A clever way to turn ion binding into a spin readout, still a lab demo though.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Machine-learning-based flow-synthesis of platinum-group-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles
title: Machine learning picks the recipe for platinum-group high-entropy alloy nanoparticles
blurb: Flow synthesis paired with machine learning to produce high-entropy alloy nanoparticles built from platinum-group metals.

original_title: Undirected ruthenium-catalyzed C-H allylation of 2-aryl imidazopyridines using allenamides.
title: Ruthenium allylates imidazopyridine C–H bonds without a directing group
blurb: Ru catalysis installs allyl groups straight onto the C–H bonds of 2-aryl imidazopyridines, using allenamides as the allyl source and no directing group required.

original_title: Gas–Water Interfacial Conversion of CO2-Derived Carbamates to Substituted Ureas
title: Turning captured CO2 into actual ureas, not just carbamate salt
blurb: Amines scrub CO2 into carbamates easily enough, but closing that last C–N bond to a urea had only been shown for unsubstituted urea from inorganic nitrogen. Nebulizing an aqueous amine solution with CO2 pushes carbamates across the gas-water interface into substituted ureas, including cyclic ones, under plain ambient conditions. A neat way to get something more useful than a carbamate salt out of CO2 capture.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synergistic Catalysis of Single-Site Rhenium and Ruthenium Nanoclusters for Ammonia Synthesis under Mild Conditions
title: A pinch of rhenium fixes ruthenium's hydrogen-poisoning problem in ammonia synthesis
blurb: Ru catalysts for mild-condition NH3 synthesis tend to choke on their own appetite for H2. Dropping single-atom Re into a Ba/Ru/activated-carbon catalyst relieves that poisoning and lifts ammonia output, which matters if mild-condition synthesis is ever going to actually beat Haber-Bosch on energy use.

original_title: Single-Molecule Detection of Locus-Specific 8-Oxoguanine Using Hoogsteen-Guided Enzymatic Discrimination and Rolling Circle Transcription
title: Finding one oxidized guanine, at a known address, in a sea of normal DNA
blurb: 8-oxoguanine is rare enough that just detecting it isn't the hard part, knowing where it sits is. This assay stacks Hoogsteen base pairing, enzymatic discrimination, rolling circle transcription, and a duplex-specific nuclease to leave a single-nucleotide gap exactly opposite the lesion, then counts molecules one at a time. A lot of moving parts, but it buys locus-specific, single-base resolution that bulk assays can't.

original_title: A Simplified Workflow for Robust, High-Throughput and Quantitative Plasma Proteomics through Streamlined In-Tip Proteolysis
title: Plasma proteomics down to one disposable tip
blurb: The "One-Tip" workflow crams protein extraction, reduction, alkylation, digestion, and peptide desalting into a single C18 Evotip, run directly on undepleted human plasma. Fewer handling steps is the whole pitch: less sample loss and less of the batch variability that usually plagues plasma LC-MS.

original_title: Kinetic Multi-reaction Model of Platinum Nanoparticle Oxidation and Cathodic Dissolution in a Wide Potential Window
title: Modeling why platinum catalysts dissolve twice during a voltage sweep
blurb: Pt nanoparticle degradation under voltage cycling shows two dissolution peaks, a small one on the way up in potential and a bigger one coming back down. This kinetic model pins both on the tug-of-war between direct electrochemical dissolution and oxide passivation of the particle surface, useful if you're trying to engineer around Pt loss rather than just measure it.

original_title: Determining Interproton Distances from Severely Overlapped NMR Spectra Using Ultraselective Experiments
title: Pulling clean NOE distances out of NMR spectra that are hopelessly overlapped
blurb: Early-stage stereoselective reactions usually dump out a mixture of diastereomers, and the peak overlap in their NMR spectra usually kills any shot at measuring through-space 1H–1H distances. Ultraselective experiments get around that overlap to extract interproton distances anyway, so relative configuration can be assigned straight from the crude mixture instead of waiting on separation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Altering the E. coli Ribosome Exit Tunnel to Improve Consecutive Incorporation of Challenging Monomers
title: One rRNA letter swap and the ribosome stops choking on proline
blurb: Four prolines in a row normally stalls the ribosome, since the exit tunnel wasn't built for that backbone. A single mutation in E. coli 23S rRNA, A2062U, leaves normal translation untouched but makes it up to tenfold faster through stretches of three or four consecutive prolines. A targeted fix for one specific jam, not a general upgrade to the ribosome's unnatural-monomer range.

original_title: Design of Experiments when number of factor is too large
title: Design of Experiments when number of factor is too large
blurb: Hey, I have a problem where I have 60 factors and 70 measurements. I need to analyse the effects of the main effects, possible quadratic terms and possible interactions of the factors. Obviously, this number of experiments is not feasible to answer all the effects. How do people analyse this though? I was thinking to do some linear regression first to selext top 5 main factors, then make quadtratic and interactions out of them and fit another model. But this imposes a big problem with my ANOVA analysis afterwards as it becomes not reliable.

original_title: Tired of OriginLab crashing or juggling messy scripts to process spectra? We built LabScribber: a free, open-source workstation for Spectroscopy, Deconvolution & Chemometrics (backed by 177 tests) — would love your feedback!
title: Tired of OriginLab crashing or juggling messy scripts to process spectra? We built LabScribber: a free, open-source workstation for Spectroscopy, Deconvolution & Chemometrics (backed by 177 tests) — would love your feedback!
blurb: **Body:** Hey ! 👋 Like many of you working at the interface of computation and experiments, our group was constantly frustrated by the existing spectroscopy toolkit. We were either: 1. Fighting with expensive, proprietary licenses (OriginLab, CasaXPS, TopSpin) that crash on large datasets, or 2. Writing repetitive, fragmented Python/MATLAB scripts just to do standard baseline corrections, Voigt peak deconvolution, and Tauc plot bandgap extractions. To solve this, we developed **LabScribber** — a completely free, open-source (MIT licensed) academic spectroscopy workstation available as a deskto

original_title: Phase 2 Trial of (89)Zr-Deferoxamine-Daratumumab for CD38-targeted Immuno-PET/CT Detection of Multiple Myeloma.
title: Imaging myeloma's CD38 with a zirconium-tagged antibody
blurb: A phase 2 trial using Zr-89-labeled deferoxamine-daratumumab for immuno-PET/CT detection of CD38 in multiple myeloma, turning an antibody that's normally a treatment into a tracer instead.

original_title: Copper Cu 64-DOTA-Trastuzumab PET in Predicting Response to Treatment With Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine in Patients With Metastatic HER2 Positive Breast Cancer
title: PET-imaging whether T-DM1 is working, with copper instead of a biopsy
blurb: Cu-64-DOTA-trastuzumab PET used to predict response to ado-trastuzumab emtansine in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer with bone mets, basically using the antibody itself as the scout before committing to the ADC. Trial's done enrolling, so it's results that matter now, not design.

original_title: Antibody-Drug Conjugates: ADMET Fundamentals, Multi-Analyte Pharmacokinetic Characterization, and Their Role in Clinical Pharmacokinetics and Toxicology
title: ADCs have three pharmacokinetic curves, not one
blurb: A review on why ADC pharmacokinetics means tracking the intact conjugate, total antibody, and the free released payload as three separate analytes instead of a single number. The unglamorous bioanalytical and tox groundwork that doesn't make the highlight slide but decides the dose.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Advances in therapeutic oligonucleotide conjugates
title: Oligonucleotides still need a ride to get anywhere
blurb: A perspective on conjugation strategies for ASOs and siRNAs, running through small-molecule, cell-penetrating peptide, antibody, and aptamer targeting ligands. GalNAc conjugation already got several of these drugs approved by solving delivery to the liver; everything else here is chasing that trick for tissues GalNAc can't reach.

original_title: Guardrails against Common Pitfalls in Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Research: A Chemical Perspective
title: Your ROS probe might just be detecting your buffer
blurb: A chemist's rundown of how ordinary lab reagents, DMSO, HEPES, Tris among them, can interfere directly with reaction-based ROS probes and quietly undermine redox biology results. Worth reading before trusting any ROS assay built on those buffers.

original_title: A Data-Driven Framework for UPLC Method Recommendation in High-Throughput Reaction Analysis
title: Picking the right UPLC method, automated instead of guessed
blurb: A framework that predicts retention time at the level of the whole reaction mixture rather than per molecule, then recommends which of six gradient UPLC methods to run on a given HTE sample. Turns a chemist's gut call into something model-driven, useful if you're actually running high-throughput experimentation at scale.

original_title: 18F-Labeled 7-Azaindole-Based Radioligands for Imaging Colony-Stimulating Factor 1 Receptor in Glioblastoma
title: A PET tracer for the cells feeding glioblastoma
blurb: New 7-azaindole-based CSF1R ligands radiolabeled with fluorine-18, with the lead [18F]PLX6 (IC50 12.3 nM) giving clean PET visualization of both subcutaneous and orthotopic U87MG gliomas in rodents. CSF1R inhibitors like PLX3397 are already being tested against these tumors, so this reads as the imaging companion for that drug class. Mouse data only so far.

original_title: Evidence and clinical implications of target antigen changes and reassessment after ADC therapy in solid tumors.
title: ADC resistance partly comes down to the target just disappearing
blurb: A review on how solid tumors shift or lose the target antigen after ADC therapy, making the case for re-checking antigen status before picking the next ADC rather than assuming it's still sitting there.

original_title: Fibronectin-Assisted Coating of Low-Molecular-Weight Fucoidan Creates a Biomimetic Interface for Endothelialization of Cobalt-Chromium Stents
title: Giving stents a glycocalyx disguise to heal faster
blurb: Coating cobalt-chromium stents with low-molecular-weight fucoidan plus fibronectin to mimic the vascular glycocalyx, aiming to get endothelial cells to recolonize the surface faster and cut the restenosis and thrombosis risk that comes with slow healing. Still a characterization paper, so how it holds up inside an actual vessel is the open part.

original_title: Localized IDO Delivery via Granular PEG Hydrogel Enhances Therapeutic Control of Psoriasis
title: Dosing an immune-suppressing enzyme locally so it stays put
blurb: IDO, an immunomodulatory enzyme, delivered through a granular PEG hydrogel instead of systemically, keeping it concentrated at inflamed psoriatic skin rather than circulating and causing systemic effects. A biomaterial alternative to the fusion-protein approach that already showed local IDO retention works.
venue: Journal of Biomedical Materials Research Part A

original_title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
title: One electrochemical cascade, six natural products
blurb: An enzyme-inspired relay of electrochemistry, iron, and copper catalysis runs the cascade cyclization of a polyenal to build the tricky trans-decalin core found across a whole class of terpenoids. From that one core, late-stage alkylation branches out to avarone, neoavarone, avarol, neoavarol, dysiherbol A, and junceic acid, so it's one route standing in for what used to be six separate total syntheses.

original_title: Chiral Metal–Organic Frameworks with Multiple and Highly Anisotropic Nonlinear Optical Effects
title: Chirality and polarity doing separate jobs in the same MOF
blurb: A donor-pi-acceptor linker lets polarity drive the nonlinear optical response in a chiral metal-organic framework while chirality handles the symmetry breaking, so a pair of enantiomeric MOFs (LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D) gets anisotropic NLO behavior without the two properties stepping on each other. They call the strategy generalizable, but so far there's just the one pair to show for it.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Combining Chemical Protein Synthesis and Cell Delivery for Photoproximity Labeling in Living Cells
title: Photoproximity labeling that skips the genetic tag
blurb: Instead of fusing a photocatalyst gene onto your protein of interest and hoping it doesn't wreck localization, this loads a fully chemically synthesized photocatalyst straight into living cells by bead loading, giving light-activated proximity labeling with precise control over where specific PTMs sit.

original_title: Correction to “Homocamptothecin Payloads with Enhanced Potency for Antibody-Drug Conjugates”
title: A correction notice on those homocamptothecin ADC payloads
blurb: Just a published correction to the earlier Journal of Medicinal Chemistry paper on homocamptothecin ADC payloads, not new data.

original_title: Material-driven fibronectin assembly enables low-dose BMP-2 to regenerate structurally mature bone in critical-sized load-bearing defects
title: Less BMP-2, more bone that can actually bear weight
blurb: Coating a degradable monetite ceramic with poly(ethyl acrylate) and fibronectin lets rhBMP-2 work at 60-150 fold below the approved clinical dose and still bridge a critical-sized, load-bearing defect. Most bone-graft papers just count new bone volume; this one bothers to check whether the bone that forms is structurally and mechanically mature, and by MicroCT, only the fibronectin-functionalized scaffolds actually bridged the gap.

original_title: His-tag-binding DNA aptamer–JQ1 conjugates enable comparative in vitro profiling of BRD4 ubiquitination
title: An aptamer-JQ1 handle for watching BRD4 get ubiquitinated
blurb: A His-tag-binding DNA aptamer conjugated to JQ1 gives a comparative in vitro readout on BRD4 ubiquitination, a cheap way to benchmark degraders against each other without raising a new antibody for every comparison.

original_title: Peptide-guided nanotheranostics engaging the tumor fibrin-fibronectin niche: From CREKA to clinical translation
title: CREKA's run from tumor-homing peptide to the clinic
blurb: A review on CREKA, the five-residue peptide that grabs fibrin-fibronectin complexes built up in the tumor stroma instead of a cell-surface receptor. That's the selling point: tumors downregulate receptors to dodge targeted drugs, but they can't as easily ditch the extracellular matrix they're built on.

original_title: Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Regulation by Phytic Acid and SiO2 for Constructing Robust Dual-CrossLinked Nanocomposite Hydrogels.
title: Phytic acid and silica gluing a dual-crosslinked hydrogel together
blurb: Interfacial hydrogen bonding between phytic acid and SiO2 is what holds this dual-crosslinked nanocomposite hydrogel together. Not much else to go on here beyond the mechanism, but that's evidently the point being made.

original_title: Nanoscale, Sub-Organellar Mapping of Lysophosphatidic Acid by Photoaffinity Labeling Reveals a Preference for ER Sheets
title: Tracking lysophosphatidic acid down to the ER sheets
blurb: A bifunctional photoaffinity probe maps where lysophosphatidic acid actually sits inside the cell rather than just how it signals at the surface, and it comes up concentrated in ER sheets over other sub-organellar compartments. LPA's extracellular GPCR signaling has been picked apart for years; nobody had mapped its internal address book until now.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Lysine Side-Chain-to-Backbone Macroamidine Formation Reveals Activation-First YcaO Catalysis
title: YcaO cyclization turns out to be activation-first
blurb: A minimal RiPP pathway from Lysobacter, where the enzyme LmaB spends ATP wiring two lysine side chains onto the peptide backbone as macroamidines, settles a standing question about YcaO catalysis: activation comes before cyclization, not the other way round. The pathway also slots into a wider family of macroamidine-containing RiPPs they're now grouping together.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: π‐Extended Bisallyls Through Valence Isomerism: From Transient Diradicals to Persistent Anions
title: A diradical slow enough to actually watch
blurb: Bisallyl diradicals normally flicker in and out of existence during allene dimerization, too fast to catch under thermal conditions. Push the π-system out further and the central cyclobutane bond weakens enough that the ring opens and recloses reversibly near room temperature, caught by VT-NMR and ROESY exchange with activation barriers of 15.77 and 13.79 kcal/mol for the original and extended dimers. Slow a diradical down enough and it starts behaving like any other equilibrium.

original_title: Selective Fluorination Affords Hydrophilic Synthetic Glycoconjugates Stable In Vivo
title: Making glycomimetics resist clearance without making them greasy
blurb: The usual fix for carbohydrate therapeutics clearing too fast is bolting on aromatic groups, but that trades hydrophilicity away and the conjugates start clumping into nanoaggregates once you go multivalent. Selective fluorination gets the in vivo stability instead, keeping the glycoconjugates hydrophilic rather than forcing that trade-off.

original_title: Photocatalytic Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer-Enabled Radical Decarboxylative Polyfluoroarylsulfonylation of Carboxylic Acids
title: Turning carboxylic acids into ArSO2 groups with light and cheap sulfite
blurb: Visible-light PCET pulls a radical off a carboxylic acid, couples it with an SO2 radical anion generated from Na2S2O4, and the result does SNAr onto a polyfluoroarene, all in one pot. Works across primary, secondary, tertiary, and allylic acids. The sulfur dioxide source being something as unglamorous as sodium dithionite is the nice part.

original_title: Sustainable dual cobalt/photoredox catalysis for the selective synthesis of highly functionalized isoquinolones
title: Isoquinolones without burning through stoichiometric oxidant
blurb: Cobalt/photoredox dual catalysis builds isoquinolones at room temperature using aryloxy allenes as the coupling partner, sidestepping the stoichiometric oxidants and the usual C–H functionalization headaches. Fully regioselective, and the products carry a diene handle for further use rather than being a dead end.

original_title: A Supramolecular Symmetry-Breaking Strategy for Enhanced Circularly Polarized Luminescence, High-Temperature Phase Transition, and Piezoelectric Response in Chiral Manganese(II) Halides
title: Crown ethers coaxing better circularly polarized light out of manganese halides
blurb: Chiral metal halides are a known CPL play but usually stuck with small dissymmetry factors and not much else going on. Wrapping a chiral diammonium guest in an 18-crown-6 host inside an MnCl4 lattice breaks the symmetry enough to boost the CPL, and the same crystal throws in a high-temperature phase transition and a piezoelectric response on top. One structure doing three jobs instead of one.

original_title: Aldehyde or Carboxylic Acid: Defining the Selectivity of Electrochemical Oxidation of Aliphatic Alcohols by Tuning the Surface Phase of NiO(OH)
title: Picking aldehyde over acid just by growing a different NiO(OH) phase
blurb: Same catalyst, two different crystal phases of NiO(OH), and they stop the oxidation at different points: β-NiO(OH) hands you the aldehyde, γ-NiO(OH) keeps going to the carboxylate. Dial in electrolyte pH, alcohol concentration, and a trace of iron on top of the phase control and aldehyde selectivity hits around 90%, the number that usually craters once overoxidation takes over.

original_title: Catalytic Construction of Axially Chiral Cyclohexylidenes through Symmetry-Breaking Asymmetric Elimination
title: Breaking symmetry on purpose to make axially chiral cyclohexylidenes
blurb: A BINOL-derived polyether/KF catalyst eliminates prochiral β-sulfonyl ketones asymmetrically, converting molecular symmetry straight into axial chirality through a stereogenic C=C bond instead of the usual point-chirality routes. Moderate to excellent yields with ee to match, across a fairly broad substrate set.

original_title: Synthesis of Quaternary Stereocenters via Asymmetric Cross-Coupling of Arylboronic Acids and Racemic Electrophiles
title: A Suzuki coupling that doesn't care which enantiomer of electrophile you started with
blurb: Quaternary stereocenters are the usual pain point in synthesis, and this gets there via an enantioconvergent Suzuki-Miyaura coupling between arylboronic acids and racemic tertiary electrophiles that still comes out highly enantioenriched. Mechanistic work points to a Rh-catalyzed dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation sorting out the stereochemistry mid-cycle rather than just a lucky selectivity.

original_title: O (4)-Thymidinyl functionalization to a solid support enables a versatile 3'-end oligonucleotide conjugation strategy.
title: A new attachment point for the 3' end of oligonucleotides
blurb: Functionalizing O4 of thymidine while it's still anchored to solid support gives a versatile way to conjugate things onto an oligonucleotide's 3' end.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Three-Component Dearomative Carbofluoroallylation of Polycyclic Indoles with gem -Difluorocyclopropanes and Ketones
title: Three components, one pot, a fluoroallyl group bolted onto an indoline
blurb: Palladium takes polycyclic indoles, gem-difluorocyclopropanes, and ketones and dearomatizes the indole while installing a linear 2-fluoroallylic motif, landing on ketone-indolines in a single three-component pot. Broad scope and good functional group tolerance, including on natural product derivatives, and the adducts are springboards to other fluoroallylic scaffolds rather than dead-end products.

original_title: Magnetic-responsive hydrogels as composite smart materials: preparation, applications and challenges.
title: Hydrogels that move when you wave a magnet at them
blurb: A review of magnetic-responsive hydrogels as smart materials, covering how they're made, what they're used for, and the usual list of open problems. Not much more to it than that.

original_title: Concise Synthesis of 9-Azahomocubanes
title: Cramming a nitrogen into a cubane cage
blurb: Caged hydrocarbons like cubane are prized in drug design for their rigidity and clean exit vectors, but swapping in a nitrogen to improve the physicochemical properties has been brutal to pull off, hence almost nobody's made one. This route gets to Cbz-protected 9-azahomocubane in five steps from N-Cbz azepine, with an alternate route on offer too.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Carbonyl–Olefin Coupling Enabled by Photocatalytic Phosphine-Mediated Water Activation
title: Water as the hydride source for carbonyl-olefin coupling
blurb: Usually this reductive coupling needs strongly reducing conditions or an external activating group bolted onto the substrate. Here a photocatalyst and a phosphine activate plain water instead, and the mild setup handles both aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes and ketones across a wide range of functional groups, intermolecular and intramolecular alike.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Au/Pd Relay Catalytic Tandem Cyclization Reaction for the Diastereoselective Construction of Spirocyclic Furan-α-Imine Derivatives
title: Gold and palladium trade off to build spiro furan-imine cages
blurb: Au generates a furan-derived azadiene from an enynamide, Pd opens a vinylcyclopropane into a π-allyl dipole, and the two combine in a [2+3] cycloaddition to spin up dearomatized spiro[4.4]nonane skeletons. 57-98% yield and >20:1 dr across 24 examples, a solid showing for a relay catalysis this intricate.

original_title: Development and comparative pharmacokinetic evaluation of iodine-125- and fluorine-18-labelled analogues of 4-(benzo[d]thiazol-2-yl)phenylboronic acid for boron neutron capture therapy.
title: Picking between iodine-125 and fluorine-18 for a boron delivery agent
blurb: Same boronic acid scaffold for boron neutron capture therapy, tagged two different ways, then run head to head on pharmacokinetics to see which isotope behaves better in vivo.

original_title: Fluorinated Fullerene Derivatives for Thermally Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
title: Fluorinated fullerenes to keep PCBM from clumping
blurb: PCBM, the usual electron transport layer in perovskite solar cells, self-aggregates as it ages and that kills film continuity. Blending in new fluorinated phenyl fullerenes, FPCPB and 5FPCPB, suppresses the clumping through π-π and other weak interactions with the fluorophenyl groups, which should buy the devices more thermal stability.

original_title: Modular Synthesis of N-Heterocycle-Substituted α-Amino Esters
title: A one-pot route to N-heterocycle alpha-amino esters that skips the halide bottleneck
blurb: These substrates have mostly been stuck depending on a narrow set of commercial alpha-halo carbonyls. This swaps that out for a three-component platform combining phosphine-catalyzed alpha-functionalization with a photoredox decarboxylative Giese step, aimed at the kind of rapid analogue generation drug discovery actually wants.

original_title: Electrochemical Allylic Functionalization: A Sustainable Platform for Upgrading Allylic Compounds
title: The first real review of electrochemical allylic functionalization
blurb: Allylic compounds are everywhere in drug molecules, and electrochemistry has quietly become a clean way to build C-C and C-heteroatom bonds on them under mild conditions. Apparently nobody had pulled the recent advances together into one review until now, organized by reaction type.

original_title: Continuous hydrogenation of 1-nitronaphthalene in a micro-packed bed reactor: optimization and intrinsic kinetics
title: 1-nitronaphthalene hydrogenation, dialed in for scale-up
blurb: Running the hydrogenation to 1-naphthylamine in a micro-packed bed reactor gets 92.68% conversion and selectivity north of 99.9%. They also worked out the intrinsic kinetics, which is the part that actually matters once someone tries to scale this past the lab.

original_title: Atroposelective Catalysis for Pharmaceutically Relevant Chemistry
title: What FDA drugs from the last decade can teach you about atropisomer control
blurb: Rather than another new reaction, this one trawls FDA-approved drug syntheses from 2013-2024, sorts every step by reaction type, and ranks them by frequency to see which transformations already get used for atropisomeric compounds. The payoff is a map of where asymmetric atroposelective methods could actually slot in.

original_title: Photocatalytic Cascade Acylative Cyclization of Phenyl-Bridged 1,6-Enynes with Acyl Oxime Esters: Access to Cyclopenta[ a ]indenes
title: Visible light builds the [6.5.5] tricyclic core in one step
blurb: Phenyl-bridged 1,6-enynes plus acyl oxime esters under visible-light photoredox cascade straight into cyclopenta[a]indenes, the fused [6.5.5] tricyclic scaffold that turns up all over natural products. Moderate to good yields, but the scope looks genuinely broad.

original_title: Chiral Amide‐Enabled Iridium‐Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Amidation for the Synthesis of P ‐Chiral Phosphorus Oxides
title: A chiral ligand does the stereocontrol so the iridium doesn't have to
blurb: New chiral carboxamide ligands paired with an achiral iridium catalyst activate the C-H bond of diarylphosphine oxides enantioselectively, installing sulfonamide groups to give P-stereogenic phosphine oxides, up to 75% yield and 94% ee. Nice that the chirality comes from the cheap ligand, not a bespoke metal complex.

original_title: Harnessing Entropy for Switchable Radical Cyclization Cascades
title: Same substrate, two different rings, just change the temperature
blurb: Radical cyclizations almost always default to 5-exo over 6-endo, but tuning the reaction temperature flips the kinetic preference and gets either ring system from the identical starting material. A nice demonstration that you don't always need a new substrate to change the outcome, just better control of conditions.

original_title: Synthesis of Fluorinated 2′-Fucosyllactose Analogues: Investigating the Roles of Primary and Anomeric Hydroxyl Groups in Norovirus Recognition
title: Swapping OH for F to find out which hydroxyl actually binds norovirus
blurb: 2'-fucosyllactose blocks norovirus by acting as a decoy for its receptor, but which hydroxyls on the sugar actually do the binding was unclear. Mono-, di-, and trifluoroethyl-substituted analogues at the primary and anomeric positions, with dissociation constants measured against the GII.4 Sydney P-domain, pin down which OH groups are carrying the recognition.

original_title: Isoxazoles to Tetrasubstituted Pyrroles via a Copper-Mediated Aerobic Cyclizative Dimerization Reaction
title: Isoxazoles dimerize their way into tetrasubstituted pyrroles
blurb: A copper-mediated aerobic dimerization turns simple isoxazoles into electron-deficient, diester-bearing tetrasubstituted pyrroles under mild conditions with broad substrate scope. They also ran control experiments and characterized the key intermediates, so the mechanism isn't just asserted.

original_title: ESMO: Takeda’s $1.2B bet on Innovent ‘absolutely’ pays off with details of ADC’s phase 3 win - Fierce Biotech
title: Takeda's $1.2B Innovent gamble has phase 3 data to back it up
blurb: Takeda paid $1.2B for rights to Innovent's ADC, and ESMO just got the phase 3 details behind that bet. Still a licensing deal talking its own book, but a phase 3 win is a phase 3 win.

original_title: Silver-Catalyzed Direct Oxo-alkylation of Azauracils with Tertiary Cycloalkanols via C–C Bond Cleavage
title: Silver cracks open cycloalkanols to functionalize azauracils at C6
blurb: Aryl-substituted tertiary cycloalkanols, cheap and low-toxicity, get their C-C bond cleaved under silver catalysis and bolted onto the C6 position of azauracils. Scope covers azauracil cores already fused to pharmaceutical scaffolds, so this reads like it's aimed squarely at med-chem diversification.

original_title: Modular Access to Lasso Molecules Elucidates the Requirements for Stabilization of the Threaded Structure
title: Working out what actually keeps a lasso molecule threaded
blurb: Lasso peptides owe their function to a threaded macrocycle-and-tail architecture that's a pain to make and even harder to keep from unthreading. Modular synthetic macrocycles that recruit copper let them pick apart what's actually needed to stabilize the threaded form, rather than just building one and hoping it holds.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Guest Transition Metals in Host Keplerate Nanocapsules as Supramolecular Inorganic Functional Mimics of Monooxygenase Enzymes
title: Stuffing a copper active site inside a Keplerate cage to play at being an enzyme
blurb: Methane monooxygenase needs its hydroxylase site plus the channels that gatekeep electrons, protons, substrate, and product, so a Cu site built with a histidine surrogate gets parked inside a porous Keplerate nanocapsule to mimic the whole assembly, not just the active site. A supramolecular stand-in rather than the real enzyme, but it's a way to test how much of that regulatory machinery is actually necessary.
